subject: Cyclone Labs — capacity healthcheck, rightsize + short-term top-up
body:
From: Alex Duarte <alex@cyclonelabs.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cyclonelabs.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity refresh: Cyclone Labs renewal sizing + surge runway

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the Q2 runbook review. We've attached a CSV export of our token-level usage for Q2 (summary + minute-level spikes). Two things we're trying to sort ahead of renewal:

- We saw three short high-concurrency spikes in June that drove sustained queueing for a few hours (attached markers).
- Our product team expects an organic feature-driven surge in Sept with heavy inference for multimodal prompt expansion.

Given those, we want to understand the minimal committed capacity to keep latency SLOs for our core routes and a pragmatic plan for a short-term top-up/burst pool rather than a large permanent commit. Can Redwood outline:

1) A steady-state commit that covers 95th percentile active tokens (you can use the CSV)
2) A burst/top-up plan (duration, provisioning lead time, and price) for expected Sept surge
3) Any quick config recommendations (batching/quantization) that materially reduce GPU needs without changing model quality

We'd like a proposal and a rough calendar so procurement can review and we can get to a DocuSign amendment if we agree.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Duarte
Head of Platform
Cyclone Labs

---

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alex Duarte <alex@cyclonelabs.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity refresh: Cyclone Labs renewal sizing + surge runway

Alex — thanks for the data and the clear asks. Quick reply with next steps:

- I'm scheduling a 30-min sizing call with Sean to walk through the CSV and confirm peak window definitions (proposed: Fri 2027-07-30 10:00 PT).
- We'll produce two concrete proposals: (A) steady-state commit + 24/7 small burst pool with auto-burst; (B) conservative steady commit + short-term top-up tranche (2-4 week) timed to your Sept feature launch.
- Early wins we can apply immediately: enable prefix KV caching on your chat routes and a recommended quantization profile for the multi-turn generator; those often reduce required GPU by ~15% without visible quality regressions.

I'll loop in Sean for the sizing details and Ben for procurement/ops scheduling once we align on the option.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Alex Duarte <alex@cyclonelabs.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity refresh: Capacity proposals for Cyclone Labs

Alex / Olga — hi, Sean from Solutions Eng. I pulled the CSV and ran a quick utilization projection. High-level options (ballpark numbers, subject to confirmation on the call):

Option A — Steady + Managed Burst
- Steady commit: equivalent of 12 A100-like slots (optimised kernels, quantized where safe) sized to ~95th percentile sustained throughput.
- Burst pool: 4 extra slots available with 15-minute auto-provisioning; can be restricted by route.
- Lead time to provision burst: 6 business hours for cloud regions (shorter if pre-approved).
- Cost: steady = committed monthly rate; burst billed at a premium hourly rate when used.

Option B — Small steady + top-up tranche
- Steady commit: 8 slots (covers median traffic).
- Short-term top-up: 8 additional slots for a 2–4 week window during Sept feature release; full capacity shift for the window.
- Lead time: 2–3 business days for tranche provisioning and routing changes.
- Cost: top-up priced as a time-limited addendum with an overall blended monthly commitment for the quarter.

Immediate operational recommendations:
- Turn on prefix/KV caching for the 0.6x of calls that repeat across sessions.
- Enable an inference quantization profile we tested internally (Q4 -> int8-like) for non-critical routes.
- Add a routed fallback to a cost-tiered model for batch workloads.

I'll put together a short table with exact slot counts by sequence-length bucket and a runbook for switching between modes. Olga — once Alex confirms the preferred option, Ben can take the SOW/amendment forward.

—Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Duarte <alex@cyclonelabs.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Katie Wu <katie.wu@cyclonelabs.com>, procurement@cyclonelabs.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity refresh: Cyclone Labs — choose option

Thanks Sean/Olga — we reviewed both options internally. We want Option A (steady + managed burst) with a caveat: can we start with a 2-week top-up period in Sept to validate our traffic and then flip the burst policy to a smaller always-on buffer? Procurement is asking for an amendment that shows the blended monthly cost for the first quarter after renewal and the hourly premium for burst usage.

Next steps from our side: procurement will review the amendment. If Redwood can give a proposed DocuSign amendment and the cost table for the two tiers (steady + burst premium), we can target an execution the week of Aug 23.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex
Head of Platform, Cyclone Labs

---

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alex Duarte <alex@cyclonelabs.com>, Katie Wu <katie.wu@cyclonelabs.com>, procurement@cyclonelabs.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cyclone Labs — capacity healthcheck, rightsize + short-term top-up

Alex / Katie / procurement — attaching the redlined amendment and a one-page cost summary for Option A (steady + managed burst). Key callouts:

- Steady commit: 12 slots (A100-equivalent) — starts on renewal effective date.
- Initial Sept validation: we will pre-provision an 4-slot top-up pool for a 2-week window starting Sept 1; after validation we will automatically transition to a smaller always-on 2-slot buffer unless you request otherwise.
- Burst lead time and throttles: 15-minute provisioning with routing constraints; billable at 1.7x the committed unit rate while active.
- Cancellation/rollback: standard 30-day amendment notice for changes to steady commit; top-up window is fixed once provisioned.

Ben (cc'd) will coordinate the internal ops schedule and confirm exact start times; procurement, if this looks good please reply with the preferred signatory and we'll send the DocuSign link.

Attachments: proposed_amendment_redwood_draft_20270820.pdf, cyclone_usage_export_2027Q2.csv
